sentences.text: Palagiri Suryanarayana Raju vs The State Of Telangana And

Another on 15 April, 2024
 The Honourable Smt. Justice K. Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.102 of 2022
Order:

This criminal petition is filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 under Section 482 Cr.P.C, to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.950 of 2012 on the file of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Nirmal, wherein the petitioner was charged with the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 IPC.
2.

entities.text:
Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Nirmal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts of the case are that the marriage of the petitioner with the 2nd respondent was performed on 16.02.2008.
At the time of marriage the parents of 2nd respondent gave 20 lakhs cash, 30 tolas of gold and 5 Kg of silver to the petitioner in addition to Rs.50,000/- to the sister of the petitioner.

After marriage, the petitioner and 2nd respondent had matrimonial life at Hyderabad for three months during which the family members of the petitioner have harassed the 2nd respondent physically and mentally demanding dowry of Rs.10 lakhs failing which she will not be taken to the USA by the petitioner.
The charge sheet does not disclose any incriminating details or incidents against the petitioner/accused No.1.
The trial of the case has not commenced so far and the statements of the witnesses do not disclose any incriminating circumstances against the petitioner.

The 2nd respondent filed divorce petition in O.P.No.286 of 2012 dated 21.07.2012 and there are no dates or events of the alleged harassment and ill treatment accompanied by the demand for additional dowry.

The petitioner and 2nd respondent lived together only for three months after which the petitioner left for USA and the 2nd respondent is also an employee and the very fact that she has taken divorce in the year 2012 disclose there is no substance in the complaint and the petitioner is a citizen of USA and is presently residing in Atlanta City, State of Georgia, USA.
There are no children to the petitioner and 2nd respondent from out of the marriage in the year 2008.
The 2nd respondent got married again after decree of divorce in the year 2012 and thus the continuation of criminal case against the petitioner is a futile exercise.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
None appeared on behalf of 2nd respondent.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the de-facto complainant herself is not in India and the charge sheet against accused Nos.2 to 5, 8 and 9 have been quashed in Crl.P.No.14117 of 2018 by this Court.
Learned counsel submits that there is no reason to continue the case as the respondent herself is not interest in continuing the case as such prayed to quash the proceedings against this petitioner.

5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed quashing of the case stating that the petitioner is accused No.1 and the prime accused, and the proceedings against the petitioner cannot be quashed and prayed the Court to dismiss the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the rival submissions and material on record, the marriage is said to have been performed in 2008 and disputes arose in 2009 and in Crl.P.No.14117 of 2018, this Court observed that respondent No.2 alleged to have married after divorce.

The allegations are general in nature and as seen from the record they have lived together only for three months and she herself filed for divorce and divorce was granted by the Court and charge sheet was filed about nine years back and there is no representation for the 2nd respondent.
Even after filing of charge sheet, trial did not commence in the case.
Therefore, there is no useful purpose would serve in keeping the case pending when the defacto complainant is not interested in prosecuting the case.
7. In view of the same, the proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.950 of 2012 on the file of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nirmal, are hereby quashed.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nirmal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. With this direction, the petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
K. SUJANA, J 15 April, 2024 ksm THE HONOURABLE SMT.
JUSTICE K.
SUJANA
